name: Orylle

facts.text: Level 83, 40,000 health. Fights linked with Orshom Brong; drawn past 3,800 she walks home.
She throws a random raider to a fixed spot about 1,200 units back up her hall (61: 31406, 69599).
Krondon's final encounter in the raid list; a February 2003 guide put her and Orshom at fifty or more players.
That she is the 'warrior queen' of the existing bot line is Living Server writing.

story: Orylle came up out of the deep seams at the head of the thrawn ogres and took Krondon without burning it, which is the most dangerous thing anyone did in Morgana's war. She kept the hall's order and put ogres in every chair. She has no use for the old learning, but she understands a hall: a queen at the end of it, a champion at her side, a herald on the road and lords in every room below. Those who reach her are not killed at once. She seizes the boldest and hurls them back down her hall toward the door, a queen's answer to a guest who came in without leave. If they walk back, she will fight them. She has never been afraid of a crowd; she simply makes the crowd come to her one thrown man at a time, while Orshom Brong burns at her shoulder.
legend: Fifty or more, and kill her with Orshom in mind: they come together, so the cold-damage casters are on him and everyone else is on her. When she throws you, do not release and do not panic. Walk back up the hall and get in. The raids that lost to her lost because the thrown men wandered off.

loremasterTopic.text: The warrior queen of Krondon. She took the hall without burning it and put an ogre in every chair. She hurls the bold back down her hall. Walk back to her; the raids that wandered off are the ones we sing about as lost.

bookPage: Orylle does not slay a challenger who reaches her chair. She hurls him back down her hall toward the door, as a queen might sweep an unbidden guest from her hearth, and waits to see if he returns. The ogres say she has done this to a hundred men and that only the ones who walked back are worth killing. Orshom Brong stands at her shoulder through all of it, burning. They fall together or not at all.
